questions.question: What risks do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each tie to the responsible use and regulation of AI in their latest 10-K risk factors?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says concerns about the responsible use of AI may cause reputational or financial harm and liability, and may lead it to incur costs to resolve such issues [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. It says that if it offers AI solutions that draw controversy, such as ones with unintended consequences, that infringe copyright or rights of publicity, or that affect human rights, privacy or employment, or if it cannot implement effective internal policies for responsible AI development and use, it may suffer brand or reputational harm, competitive harm or legal liability [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. On regulation, NVIDIA says complying with multiple regulations from different jurisdictions may raise its cost of doing business, change how it operates, and impede its ability to offer certain products and services in some jurisdictions [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. It adds that compliance with existing and proposed AI regulation, including in the European Union, may raise research and development costs and create additional reporting or transparency requirements [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. It also says changes in AI-related regulation could disproportionately impact and disadvantage it [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. Finally, it says a failure to address responsible-use concerns and regulations could undermine public confidence in AI and slow adoption of AI in its products and services [0001045810-26-000021:0047].

On regulation, AMD says new and proposed AI legislation, and new applications of existing data protection, privacy and intellectual property laws, could expose it to competitive harm, regulatory action and legal liability [0000002488-26-000018:0052]. AMD also notes that regulatory restrictions may increasingly target products that enable or facilitate AI [0000002488-26-000018:0052]. Intel says its use of AI technology may subject it to reputational, financial, legal or regulatory risks [0000050863-26-000011:0074]. On regulation, Intel says evolving laws, rules, regulations and industry standards governing AI may require it to expend significant resources to modify, maintain or align its business practices or products [0000050863-26-000011:0074]. On September 15, 2025, China's antitrust regulators published a preliminary finding that NVIDIA's compliance with applicable U.S. export controls, which required it to offer degraded products to the Chinese market, discriminated unfairly against customers in the China market and therefore violated the terms of China's approval of the Mellanox acquisition [0001045810-26-000021:0041].
NVIDIA says that if regulators conclude it failed to fulfill the terms of the Mellanox acquisition or violated any applicable law in China, it could be subject to financial penalties, restrictions on its ability to conduct its business, restrictions or other orders regarding its networking business, products, and services, or other impacts on its operations in China [0001045810-26-000021:0041].
NVIDIA says any of these could have a material and adverse impact on its business, operating results and financial condition [0001045810-26-000021:0041].

questions.question: How does NVIDIA describe the steps it has taken to secure supply and the risks those supply commitments create, in its FY2026 10-K risk factors?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says it has long manufacturing lead times, builds finished products and holds inventory ahead of anticipated demand, and has experienced extended lead times of more than 12 months [0001045810-26-000021:0021]. To secure future supply and capacity, it has paid premiums, provided deposits, and entered into long-term supply agreements and capacity commitments, which have increased its product costs, and this may continue [0001045810-26-000021:0021]. It says it may still be unable to secure sufficient capacity commitments for its business needs [0001045810-26-000021:0021].
NVIDIA also says it continues to increase supply and capacity purchases with existing and new suppliers to support its demand projections and the growing complexity of its data center products [0001045810-26-000021:0023]. It has entered and may continue to enter into prepaid manufacturing and capacity agreements for current and future products [0001045810-26-000021:0023]. Integrating new suppliers and contract manufacturers adds complexity in managing multiple suppliers with differing production planning, execution and logistics [0001045810-26-000021:0023]. NVIDIA is also increasing its U.S.-based manufacturing and investing in specialized equipment and processes, but it may face delays or difficulties in scaling production as planned [0001045810-26-000021:0023].
On the risks, NVIDIA says that if it inaccurately estimates demand or customers change orders, it may not be able to reduce supply commitments in time, at the same rate, or at all [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. Mismatches between supply and demand have resulted in both product shortages and excess inventory and have significantly harmed its financial results, and they could reoccur [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. If it overestimates demand, it may be unable to use on-hand inventory or reduce purchase commitments [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. It has had to write down inventory, incur cancellation penalties, and record impairments, and may have to do so again [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. It also says it has incurred and may incur inventory provisions or impairments if inventory or supply or capacity commitments exceed demand [0001045810-26-000021:0023].
NVIDIA says these risks are amplified by non-cancellable and non-returnable purchase orders placed in advance of its historical lead times [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. It adds that the risks have increased and may keep increasing as purchase obligations and prepaids have grown and are expected to grow into a greater portion of total supply [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. All of these factors may negatively affect gross margins and financial results [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. Related supplier risks it lists include requirements to place non-cancellable orders or to prepay for supply in advance [0001045810-26-000021:0026]. In its MD&A, NVIDIA reports that fiscal year 2026 gross margin was also affected by a $4.5 billion charge for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations [0001045810-26-000021:0063].

questions.question: Who does NVIDIA name as its competitors in its FY2026 10-K, and what does it consider the principal competitive factors in its market?

The filing also names providers of semiconductor-based high-performance interconnect products based on InfiniBand, Ethernet, Fibre Channel and proprietary technologies as a significant source of competition [0001045810-26-000021:0012].

questions.question: What does NVIDIA say drove its revenue growth in fiscal year 2026, and what external constraints and product-transition challenges does it highlight in its FY2026 MD&A?

answer.text:
NVIDIA reports fiscal year 2026 revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% from a year ago [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. It says Data Center revenue grew 68%, driven by the major platform shifts of accelerated computing and AI [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. Within Compute & Networking, Data Center computing revenue grew 59% on demand for the Blackwell computing platform [0001045810-26-000021:0066]. Data Center networking revenue grew 142%, driven by the introduction and ramp of NVLink compute fabric for GB200 and GB300 systems and by growth of Ethernet and InfiniBand platforms [0001045810-26-000021:0066]. Gaming revenue rose 41% on strong Blackwell demand, Professional Visualization rose 70% on Blackwell demand and the launch of DGX Spark, and Automotive rose 39% on adoption of self-driving platforms [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. Graphics segment revenue growth was driven by sales of the Blackwell architecture [0001045810-26-000021:0067].
On external constraints, NVIDIA says it expects supply constraints to be a headwind to Gaming in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and beyond [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. On export controls, the USG in April 2025 required a license for exports of H20 products to China and D:5 countries, and NVIDIA incurred a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations as demand diminished [0001045810-26-000021:0062]. Licenses granted in August 2025 led to approximately $60 million in H20 revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0062]. A February 2026 license for small amounts of H200 products to China-based customers has produced no revenue so far, and NVIDIA does not know whether imports will be allowed into China [0001045810-26-000021:0062]. Any H200 shipped under that program will face a 25% tariff on import into the United States [0001045810-26-000021:0062]. NVIDIA states it was effectively foreclosed from the China data center compute market as of the end of fiscal year 2026 [0001045810-26-000021:0042]. It also notes that open-source AI, if deployed on competitors' platforms, could reduce demand for its products [0001045810-26-000021:0062]. Macroeconomic factors such as tariffs, inflation, interest rate changes and supply chain constraints affect its results, particularly demand [0001045810-26-000021:0062].
On product transition, gross margin fell to 71.1% from 75.0% as the business moved from offering Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. The $4.5 billion H20 charge also contributed to the decline [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. That charge partly offset the growth in Compute & Networking segment operating income [0001045810-26-000021:0067].

questions.question: Who does AMD identify as its main competitors in each of its segments in its FY2025 10-K?

answer.text:
In the Data Center segment, AMD says it competes primarily against Intel and Nvidia with its CPU, GPU, DPU and AI NIC server products, and against Altera with its FPGA and adaptive SoC server products [0000002488-26-000018:0014]. It adds that a variety of smaller fabless silicon companies offer proprietary accelerator solutions and Arm-based CPUs for data center use, and that some customers are developing their own data center microprocessor and accelerator products [0000002488-26-000018:0014].

questions.question: How was Intel's sale of a majority stake in Altera structured, and how did it affect Intel's FY2025 financial statements?

answer.text:
Intel signed a transaction agreement on April 14, 2025 to sell 51% of the issued and outstanding common stock of Altera, then a wholly owned subsidiary, to SLP VII Gryphon Aggregator, L.P., an affiliate of SLP [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. The sale closed on September 12, 2025 for net purchase consideration of $4.3 billion [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. That consideration consisted of $4.3 billion in cash received at closing, $500 million in deferred cash proceeds received in the third quarter of 2025, and $500 million in deferred cash proceeds payable no later than December 31, 2027 [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. It was offset by $400 million of cash transferred to Altera, about $469 million of separation and employee-related costs Intel agreed to fund to SLP, and other direct and incremental costs of the sale [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
Altera was deconsolidated effective September 12, 2025, and its results were included in Intel's "all other" category through September 11, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0039]. Intel's retained interest is accounted for under the equity method and classified within equity investments [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. At December 27, 2025 its carrying value was $3.2 billion and Intel's ownership interest was 48% [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
The sale produced a $5.6 billion pre-tax gain, recognized in interest and other, net [0000050863-26-000011:0046]. This was partly offset in that line by a $1.8 billion net loss from the change in fair value of the derivative liability for the Escrowed Shares and by $229 million of charges related to the sale of the NAND memory business [0000050863-26-000011:0046]. The 2025 effective tax rate was 98.3%, and the filing says the nonrecurring Altera gain partly offset the effect of the valuation allowance change on that rate [0000050863-26-000011:0046].
On the balance sheet at December 27, 2025, Intel had a $463 million receivable from SLP in other long-term assets for the present value of the deferred consideration [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. It also had $327 million in other accrued liabilities and $97 million in other long-term liabilities for unpaid separation and employee-related costs owed to SLP [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. Intel is still finalizing customary closing adjustments, which may change the final net cash proceeds and the gain on sale [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
"All other" revenue was $3.6 billion in 2025, down $38 million from 2024, mainly because of lower revenue from other non-reportable segments after the Altera divestiture, largely offset by higher Mobileye revenue [0000050863-26-000011:0039]. "All other" operating income was $264 million in 2025, compared with an operating loss of $57 million in 2024, helped by improved Altera operating income contribution [0000050863-26-000011:0039].
Intel also provides wafer manufacturing services to Altera, now a related party, and expects reimbursement for corporate services under a transition services agreement [0000050863-26-000011:0145].

questions.question: What did Intel's 2024 Restructuring Plan involve, and when did Intel expect it to be substantially completed, per the FY2024 10-K?

answer.text:
Intel's 2024 Restructuring Plan was announced in Q3 2024 and initiated to implement cost-reduction measures, including reductions in employee headcount, other operating expenditures, and capital expenditures [0000050863-25-000009:0123][0000050863-25-000009:0039]. The headcount actions were expected to result in an approximate 15% decrease in Intel's core workforce by early 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0021].
The restructuring charges are primarily employee severance and benefit arrangements, non-cash charges for asset impairments associated with exit activities, and charges relating to real estate exits and consolidations [0000050863-25-000009:0123]. Intel recognized restructuring charges of $2.8 billion in 2024 [0000050863-25-000009:0021], and it expects total charges of approximately $3.0 billion under the plan [0000050863-25-000009:0123].
Intel expected actions under the plan to be substantially complete by the fourth quarter of 2025, which is subject to change [0000050863-25-000009:0123][0000050863-25-000009:0039].

questions.question: What did Intel's FY2024 10-K say about its policy on dividends and stock repurchases, and what constrains its ability to return cash to stockholders?

answer.text:
Intel said it has ceased to return capital to stockholders: in recent years it has not repurchased its stock, and it reduced and then suspended its quarterly dividend in the fourth quarter of 2024 [0000050863-25-000009:0073].
Under its commercial CHIPS Act agreement, Intel agreed to forgo paying dividends for the next two years and to limits on dividend payments for the three years after that [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. Intel said there can be no assurance that it will be able to pay dividends in the future [0000050863-25-000009:0073].
On repurchases, Intel is not obligated to make repurchases under its stock repurchase program, and there can be no assurances about the amount, timing or execution of any future repurchases, or that any repurchases will enhance long-term stockholder value [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. Its last repurchase under the authorization was in Q1 2021, and no shares were repurchased during the fiscal year ending December 28, 2024 [0000050863-25-000009:0083]. As of December 28, 2024, Intel was authorized to repurchase up to $110.0 billion, of which $7.2 billion remained available [0000050863-25-000009:0084].
As of December 28, 2024, it had $51.0 billion in aggregate principal amount of senior unsecured notes and other borrowings outstanding [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. It said its debt level and debt service obligations, together with industry cyclicality and macroeconomic conditions, could reduce its flexibility to respond to changing business and economic conditions and increase the risk of credit rating downgrades [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. It also said it may need to raise additional financing for purposes including working capital, capital expenditures and debt service [0000050863-25-000009:0073].

questions.question: What is the status of the third Texas patent case and the related license defense in Intel's VLSI litigation, according to the FY2025 10-K?

answer.text:
The third Texas case went to trial in November 2022 with VLSI asserting one remaining patent, and the jury found the patent valid and infringed and awarded VLSI approximately $949 million in damages, plus interest and a running royalty [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. The court has not yet entered final judgment [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. In February 2023, Intel filed motions for a new trial and for judgment as a matter of law notwithstanding the verdict, and further appeals are possible [0000050863-26-000011:0176].
On the license defense, Intel moved in April 2024 to add the defense that it is licensed to VLSI's patents, and the court granted that motion the same month [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. In May 2025, the court held a trial on an underlying factual question relating to the license defense, and the jury returned a verdict in Intel's favor [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. Post-trial briefing is complete, and the court will address the ultimate legal issue of whether Intel obtained a license to the asserted VLSI patent through its license agreement with Finjan when Fortress Investments acquired Finjan [0000050863-26-000011:0176].
Separately, Intel's July 2024 suit in the District of Delaware seeking a finding that it is licensed to VLSI's patents was stayed in December 2024, and the Delaware court continues to receive status reports from the parties about the Texas court's consideration of the license defense [0000050863-26-000011:0177]. As of December 27, 2025, Intel had accrued a charge of approximately $1.0 billion related to the VLSI litigation and states it is unable to make a reasonable estimate of losses in excess of recorded amounts [0000050863-26-000011:0177].

questions.question: How does NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K describe the oversight and management of cybersecurity risk?

answer.text:
NVIDIA's Board of Directors oversees information security matters, including managing and assessing risks from cybersecurity threats [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. The Audit Committee reviews the adequacy and effectiveness of the company's information security policies and practices and the internal controls regarding information security risks, and it receives regular updates from management, including the Chief Security Officer and members of the security team [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. The Board also receives annual reports on information security matters from the Chief Security Officer and the security team [0001045810-26-000021:0054].
Day-to-day, security efforts are managed by a team of executive cybersecurity, IT, engineering, operations, and legal professionals [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. A cross-functional leadership team of executive-level leaders meets regularly to review cybersecurity matters and evaluate emerging threats, and it provides oversight and guidance as the information security teams refine practices to address emerging risks and regulatory changes [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. This executive leadership team also takes part in incident response by engaging with the incident response team and helping direct the company's response to and assessment of certain incidents [0001045810-26-000021:0054].
NVIDIA has designated a Chief Security Officer, who reports to the Senior Vice President of Software Engineering, to oversee the identification, assessment, and management of material cybersecurity risks [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. The filing says this officer's expertise includes over 18 years of combined government and private sector assignments [0001045810-26-000021:0054].
On risk management, the filing says the information security management programs generally follow processes outlined in frameworks such as the ISO 27001 international standard, and the company consults external parties such as cybersecurity firms and risk management and governance experts [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. Cybersecurity risk is integrated into the overall risk management systems and processes, supported by cybersecurity and data privacy training and policies [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. NVIDIA also runs a vendor risk assessment process that uses supplier questionnaires, depending on the nature and sensitivity of the supplier and the data it processes, and routinely assesses high-risk suppliers' conformance to industry standards such as ISO 27001, ISO 28001, and C-TPAT [0001045810-26-000021:0054].
